newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 6.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Household savings must become one of the most important sources of investment in the Czech Republic, according to financial experts.
- The National Property Fund has decided to sell its 13.28 percent block of shares of Later Chrudim a.s. in a public tender. The price announced was 52.244 million crowns.

- Foreign exchange reserves totalled $16.133 billion (434.6 billion crowns) at the end of September. The Czech National Bank alone held $12.633 billion (340.4 billion crowns). This is a slight decrease from the end of August when the reserves totalled $16.552 billion, though in crowns this actually represents a slight increase (from 431 billion crowns).
- Representatives of the Railway Workers Trade Union were "very unsatisfied with the results" of the meeting with the management of Czech Railways.

- Ceska Pojistovna will begin its first round of its issue of new shares tomorrow. The issue is intended to increase the insurance company's basic capital from the current 2.27 billion to 3.41 billion crowns.
- President Vaclav Havel stated that it would be good if the traditional potential of Czech arms manufacturers could be used in the equipping of the Czech army.
- Spolchemie a.s. is intending to take part in the Bulgarian privatisation process. The company is interested in obtaining a majority share in Orgachim a.s..
MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Garant pension fund has become a part of Ceska Sporitelna's group and should merge with Sporitelna's pension fund by the end of the year.
- Norddeutsche Landesbank will issue Eurobonds in Czech crowns. The volume of the issue will be one billion crowns. The two-year bonds will have a fixed interest rate of 10.85 percent.
PRAVO - According to a public survey, voters expect the Civic Democratic Party (ODS) to win the Senatorial elections.
- The National Property Fund is offering one third of Magneton Kromeriz a.s. in a public tender. -- Prague Newsroom, +42-2-2423-0003
